annotations.description: Loki has components that are down. Service unavailability can lead to potential data loss and query failures. Immediate investigation required.
Loki ingesters are failing to flush chunks to storage. This means log data is not being persisted and will be lost if ingesters restart. Immediate action required to prevent data loss.
Loki Write-Ahead Log (WAL) disk is full. This causes immediate data loss as new logs cannot be written. Urgent action required - add disk space or clean up old WAL segments.
Loki is detecting corrupt chunks or index cache corruptions. Data integrity is compromised. Investigate storage backend health and consider rebuilding affected indexes.
Loki ingester ring has unhealthy members. Ring instability affects data replication and query routing. Unhealthy ingesters may cause data loss and degraded query performance.
annotations.summary: Loki ingester ring has unhealthy members

annotations.description: Loki push latency P99 exceeds 2 seconds. High push latency affects log ingestion and can cause backpressure on log shippers. Check ingester capacity and storage backend performance.
Loki is discarding more than 100 log samples per second. This means logs are being dropped and data is missing. Check rate limits, ingester capacity, and label cardinality.

Loki is rejecting more than 50 out-of-order log entries per second. This indicates timestamp issues in log sources - logs arriving with timestamps too far in the past. Check log shipper configurations and system clocks.
Loki cache hit rate is below 50%. Low cache hit rate degrades query performance and increases load on storage backend. Consider increasing cache size or investigating query patterns.
annotations.summary: Loki cache hit rate is low

annotations.description: Loki index gateway latency P99 exceeds 1 second. Slow index queries affect all log searches and can cause query timeouts. Check index gateway resources and storage performance.
annotations.summary: Loki index gateway latency is high

annotations.description: Loki object storage latency P99 exceeds 2 seconds. Slow chunk retrieval from storage affects query performance and can cause timeouts. Check storage backend health and network connectivity.
annotations.summary: Loki object storage latency is high

annotations.description: Loki chunk age P99 exceeds 2 hours (7200 seconds). Old chunks indicate flush delays and memory pressure on ingesters. This can lead to high memory usage and potential OOM kills.
Loki ingester ring has members in LEAVING state. This may indicate intentional scale-down or unintended pod termination. Monitor for potential data redistribution issues.
annotations.summary: Loki ingester ring has leaving members

annotations.description: Loki ingester checkpoint creation is failing. Checkpoints are essential for recovery on restart - without them, ingesters may lose data or take longer to recover after a restart.
Loki ingester has more than 100,000 active streams. High stream cardinality causes memory pressure and performance issues. Review label usage and consider reducing cardinality.
